title: What Team Work Is
summary: Team work at Zura Spa is shared responsibility toward one client experience. It is not friendship, silence, or doing another person's job for them.

sections.title: The Core Idea
paragraphs: Team work is two or more people carrying a shared objective with clear individual responsibility.
At Zura Spa, that shared objective is: to work together professionally and consistently so every client receives an exceptional experience.
You do not become a team because you like one another. You become a team because the work requires coordination, trust, and a common standard.

sections.title: What Team Work Is
list: Knowing your part and completing it without waiting to be chased.
Supporting a colleague so the client never feels the gap.
Communicating early: delays, blockers, room status, client needs.
Accepting correction without treating it as an attack.
Protecting the standard even when the other person is your friend.
Synchronising in a shared session so the client feels one service, not two competing therapists.

sections.title: What Team Work Is Not
list: Covering up a colleague's mistake, lateness, or misconduct.
Doing someone else's assigned work because you do not want conflict.
Silence, gossip, or side conversations instead of a direct work update.
A clique that shares information only with favourites.
Friendship or family feeling that outranks the client.
Competition for praise, tips, or status in the massage room.

sections.title: The Therapist's Mindset
paragraphs: The correct mindset is: "I will do my part fully, and I will help the team succeed without lowering the standard."
You do not need to personally like every colleague. You do need to respect them, communicate clearly, support the session, and treat them fairly.
Warmth is welcome. Favouritism is not. Help is required. Rescue from accountability is not.

sections.title: How Team Work Shows on the Floor
paragraphs: Team work is visible in ordinary moments: a room that is ready before handover, a water request that is passed on, a 4-hands session that stays in rhythm, a report given before a problem becomes a surprise, and a disagreement that stays professional until the client has left.
list: Before the client: prepare, communicate availability, and do not leave gaps for others to discover.
During the session: follow the session leadership for that booking; protect comfort, privacy, and flow.
After the session: reset, update, and hand over facts — not complaints dressed as updates.

sections.title: Shared Work, Individual Accountability
paragraphs: A shared assignment does not erase individual responsibility.
If your part was not done, "we were doing it together" does not remove accountability.
If a colleague is struggling, help them. Then make sure the work is still completed to standard, and report honestly when something was missed.

remember: Team work is shared purpose plus individual responsibility. Support the colleague. Protect the client. Do not cover up.
